question: At an informal meeting of some EU ministers for home affairs and justice in Munich, the Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration, Magnus Brunner, announced that Frontex could take care of anti-drone operations in future. For years, the agency has been testing drone detection and neutralisation systems at the EU’s external borders to prevent smuggling and unauthorised surveillance.

A ‘Counter-Unmanned Aircraft Systems (C-UAS) Prize Contest’ currently rewards companies for such technologies. Furthermore, the Commission plans to dedicate an additional EUR 250 million from the border management fund specifically to drones. It is unclear, however, whether these funds are to go exclusively to Frontex or also to Member States and private actors.
Meanwhile, the Commission is working on a reform of Frontex’s mandate that will be presented by the end of 2026. 1.
What is the Commission’s legal basis for Frontex’s future involvement in anti-drone operations, and where could the measures take place?
For which measures will the announced EUR 250 million from the border management fund be used, and who will receive this financing (agencies, Member States or private companies)?

How much has the Commission spent to date on drones (MALE drones in Crete and Malta, VTOL drones on coastal patrol vessels, etc.) and on research and pilot projects with unmanned systems (air, land, sea)?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.1.2026) The legal basis for the involvement of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency in counter-drone measures is Regulation (EU) 2019/18961. The Agency can provide technical and operational assistance to Member States, in particular in the field of European integrated border management, which includes border control and border surveillance as components.
The Commission is expanding the support to counter the risk posed by non-cooperative drones.

The Commission plans inter alia to provide financial support to the Member States participating in the Instrument for Financial Support for Border Management and Visa Policy (BMVI)2 via the BMVI Specific Action ‘Support for border management capabilities including drones (unmanned aircraft systems (UAS)) and counter-drone measures (counterunmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS))’.

The supported measures aim to bolster the EU preparedness to counter the risk posed by non-cooperative drones in particular by focusing on the purchase of UAS and C-UAS in view of border surveillance. The Commission has been providing financial support to the Member States for purchasing drones to be used in the field of border management3, internal security4 and research and innovation5.

The funding provided to the Member States’ programmes for border management and internal security focused on reinforcing Member States’ border surveillance capabilities, including drones. Under the European Defence Fund6, the Commission cofinanced research and development projects in the area of UAS and unmanned aerial vehicles operations and detection for a total of EUR 350 million.
